bullets.title: AVGO: JPM & Wolfe both bullish on TPU pipeline; 2027 AI revenue to grow 2-2.5x
bullets.body: JPM's Harlan Sur confirms AVGO's TPU v8i 3nm 'Sunfish' fully qualified and ramping with 18+ month lead over Google's MediaTek alternative; 5-year GOOGL/AVGO agreement through TPU v11 with annual revenue commitment increases through 2031. Wolfe notes $29bn XPV residual value backstop risk but if XPV financing closes, 20-25GW FY28 target implies $250-300bn XPU revenue. AVGO targets 2027 AI revenue growth of 2-2.5x with 2028 doubling that again.

bullets.title: INTC: 18A yields 3-4 months ahead of target; CPU SAM could reach $260-300B with agentic AI
bullets.body: INTC 18A process achieving ~0.5 defect density with 40% yield and reaching industry-standard yields by year-end 2026; supply-constrained through 2027. Klein notes EMIB-T advanced packaging represents multi-$B per customer potential, and CPU SAM could expand to $260-300B as agentic AI drives demand. Board pushing for more capex in Oregon/Arizona/Ohio.

bullets.title: SNAP: Specs launch at $2,195 widely panned on form factor, battery, price vs. META Ray-Bans
bullets.body: SNAP's SPECS AR glasses launched at $2,195 with only 4-hour battery life and bulky form factor, comparing poorly to META Ray-Bans at $224-$799. Citi and MS both flag competitive disadvantage; META has EssilorLuxottica/Ray-Ban partnership and designer frames while GOOGL partners with WRBY and Gentle Monster. Stock down ~10% on launch reaction.

bullets.title: HPE: Networking revenue approaching +10% FY26; AI infrastructure demand 'extremely strong'
bullets.body: HPE Discover 2026 highlighted networking revenue growth 'approaching' +10% FY26 and +8-12% FY27, with Aruba/Juniper integration ahead of schedule. HPE is first-to-market with liquid-cooled QFX5250 1.6T switch and won design on AMD Helios rack-scale platform. GS notes deeper synergies across networking/compute/storage with meaningfully higher full-year AI revenue outlook.

bullets.title: CRM: Down 11 consecutive trading days, back to late-2018 levels; hits new 52-week low
bullets.body: CRM has fallen for 11 straight trading days—its longest losing streak ever—with minimal analyst engagement per GS. The stock is back to late-2018 price levels and is confirmed at a new 52-week low, down 38.9% over 52 weeks per StreetAccount's 52-week high/low screen. UBS also moved CRM from Most Preferred to Bellwether list.

bullets.title: MSFT: Copilot Cowork GA with usage-based pricing; 30-40% cheaper than Claude; may host DeepSeek
bullets.body: MSFT launched Copilot Cowork globally with task-based 'Copilot Credits' pricing and a multi-model strategy spanning Anthropic Opus/Sonnet, OpenAI GPT-5.5, and in-house models—positioning cost and governance as key differentiators. Internal testing shows Cowork 30-40% cheaper than Claude; MSFT is also considering hosting a DeepSeek version for further cost reduction. A $3B+ MSFT-ORCL infrastructure deal reportedly fell through on security/compliance concerns.

bullets.title: DKNG: Deposit growth +7.5% QTD vs. 4% consensus; PA May sports GGR weak but handle share gained
bullets.body: MS consumer note flags DKNG deposits tracking +7.5% QTD vs. 4% revenue growth consensus, while FanDuel tracks +5% vs. -6% consensus; combined market share stable at 70-75%. Pennsylvania May data shows DKNG sports GGR -5% YoY despite handle +12% YoY as hold collapsed 180bps; handle share expanded to 32% from 26%, and iGaming estimated -7% YoY.

bullets.title: CEG/VST/TLN: Bernstein initiates CEG & VST outperform; FERC vote tomorrow key catalyst for IPPs
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated CEG outperform with $296 PT citing nuclear fleet as 'irreplaceable physical moat' and AI/data center demand; VST initiated outperform at $181 PT on diversified dispatchable fleet. MS notes FERC meeting tomorrow addresses data center interconnection and co-location tariffs—needed for PJM to resume contracting—while TLN is outperforming on investor momentum and a request to add gas-fired generation at Montour County.

bullets.title: FSLR: Bernstein initiates underperform at $217 PT on 45X tax credit dependency
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated FSLR at underperform with $217 price target, citing the company's heavy reliance on 45X manufacturing tax credits for margins as the key risk. Stock trading down ~1-1.4% premarket on the initiation.

bullets.title: UBS IT sector update: Adds LRCX to Most Preferred; removes SNOW; NVDA stays top pick
bullets.body: UBS is neutral on US IT overall but increases semiconductor cap-ex equipment exposure, adding Lam Research to Most Preferred. NVDA remains top semiconductor pick on high-quality growth and attractive valuation. Snowflake removed from Most Preferred with coverage discontinued; INTU, PANW, CRM moved from Most Preferred to Bellwether; coverage also discontinued on EPAM, FTNT, HPE, MDB.

bullets.title: CRWV: CY26 capacity raised to 1.9GW; Nasdaq 100 inclusion June 22
bullets.body: CoreWeave capacity expectations for CY26 have been raised to 1.9GW. DeepSeek benchmark performance is being interpreted as CoreWeave having trained the model, adding a narrative catalyst. Stock joins the Nasdaq 100 on June 22.

bullets.title: DDOG: Citi raises PT to $270 from $218 post-DASH; token monetization path opens but near-term choppy
bullets.body: Citi reaffirms Buy on DDOG and lifts PT to $270 from $218 following the DASH conference, highlighting 100+ products/features launched with OTel and AI Agent monitoring as standouts. A direct monetization path via tokenization is emerging, but token scrutiny could create near-term choppiness.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: HDD pricing could double by 2028; EPS upside 35%+ YoY vs. 15-20% expected
bullets.body: Klein argues HDD pricing will double by 2028 versus company guidance, with WDC and STX EPS potentially exploding 35%+ YoY versus the 15-20% currently expected. Canadian market data shows WDC.CN trading +5.3% intraday as semis broadly rally on AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: VRT/AAON: Google Brazos liquid cooling retrofit seen as new demand catalyst
bullets.body: OPCO notes VRT, AAON, and MOD benefit from Google's Brazos liquid cooling retrofit announcement, drawing parallels to the AWS retrofit opportunity that benefited AAON last year. Higher-margin retrofit demand and durability are the key thesis despite initial stock weakness on the announcement.

bullets.title: CMI: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW; Circe Energy 2GW deal could add $0.50-$1.00 EPS by 2030
bullets.body: CMI announced an agreement with Circe Energy to supply natural gas generators for a West Texas data center campus phased 2026-2030, with potential ~2GW delivery. Morgan Stanley estimates $0.50-$1.00 EPS uplift in 2030 (vs. $51 base) if full 2GW installed, validating CMI's 130L natural gas platform for prime power data center applications at $750/kW pricing.

bullets.title: NFLX: Denies interest in Lionsgate and Roku acquisitions
bullets.body: Netflix spokesperson stated the company is 'not interested' in a Lionsgate takeover and has no plans to pursue an acquisition, contradicting a Semafor report. Netflix also clarified it did not bid for Roku; Fox separately agreed to purchase Roku.

bullets.title: DUOL: DAU tracking +21.4% YoY, ahead of consensus; monetization upside likely delays to 3Q
bullets.body: DA Davidson flags DUOL DAU at +21.4% YoY in 2Q26 vs. consensus +20.3%, with week-over-week growth the strongest in 46 weeks driven by a June streak-revival event reactivating high-engagement users. IR indicates confidence on a DAU beat and potential +5-6% upside to 2Q bookings consensus, but monetization conversion likely delays to 3Q; analyst maintains Neutral on unproven monetization and TAM saturation risk.

bullets.title: T: CFO Desroches retiring year-end; stock down ~1.5% on transition
bullets.body: AT&T CFO Pascal Desroches is retiring at year-end, to be succeeded by Jennifer Biry (former McAfee CFO); guidance was left unchanged. Stock is trading down ~1.5% premarket on the news.

bullets.title: AMZN: FTC lawsuit risk on sponsored listings; AWS selected by Southwest as preferred cloud
bullets.body: Amazon faces a potential FTC lawsuit with billions in civil penalties over alleged misrepresentation in sponsored listings disclosure and reserve pricing practices. Separately, Southwest Airlines selected AWS as its preferred cloud provider, targeting full transition from on-premises to cloud-based AI architecture by 2028.

bullets.title: UBS quant crowding: DELL +15.5 delta (most crowded long); AAPL, QCOM short crowding building
bullets.body: UBS tech crowding screens show DELL at the largest 2-week crowding delta at +15.50 (2+ std dev), with INTU also elevated at +13.29 on short-covering post-earnings. AAPL is seeing notable crowding decline at -6.11 delta and QCOM at -7.72, both signaling short crowding buildup. IBM, CSCO, and HPE show notable long crowding spikes in hardware/networking.
